notes.title: Dev Diary 23rd May 2019 - Economic Rebalance
notes.notes:
Based on player feedback, we have made better balancing the economy and the pace of growth in the game a prime priority, to this end we have released updates with a few major changes:

[h1]Household Costs and Property Revenue[/h1]
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34903694/86828dc1e08538e4849816a977a5cd70148108b3.png[/img]
We have balanced and tweaked the Household Costs a fair amount so that the issue of racing up classes automatically does not happen, and the player is faced with a more interesting challenge of managing their income much more strategically for growth.

We have also balanced the costs and revenues of most Property types to this end

[h1]Market Events[/h1]
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34903694/9c326739175c44c230b3e300a9aaeda055bf1cb7.png[/img]
We have subdued the effect of market events a little so that the deals offered are now in the 0.75x to 1.25x range which I feel gives a fair chance to still secure good deals while not being as heavily exploitable as before

[h1]Stewardship's effect on Property and Cash[/h1]
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34903694/ebad4246225f6318dffe30f1ad2c8324dbf3a6bd.png[/img]
We have introduced a soft cap on the number of items of each property type that you can effectively profit off based on the Stewardship skill of your household. The higher your effective household stewardship, more the property you can own, manage and profit from. This should better reflect the reality of having to actively manage property to turn a profit.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34903694/fbf174334c2fb816436a750d1cd7bb5a11b1475e.png[/img]
The way the calculation works is it takes your Paterfamilias Stewardship skill at full value, his wife's Stewardship at half value, the Stewardship of his children over the age of 7 at a quarter value and that of everyone else in your household at one-eight's value. It ignores the Stewardship of any characters that are busy doing something else like say studying philosophy in Greece.
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34903694/57a77022b013accff1308aa49f306c34b3ec078b.png[/img]
Similarly we now also have a cap on the amount of cash you can hoard, based again on the same Stewardship and Class calculation. The cap is high enough that you shouldn't be hitting it until you reach a fairly high class. Any cash you earn over this limit will be wasted.

We will be adding alternative places to spend your cash other than Festivals and Elections in the upcoming updates

[h1]What's next[/h1]

These changes and the numbers behind them will continue to be balanced, especially with your input. I understand that this change may make the game a bit harder for most people, but I am hoping it will continue to be challenging enough to be fun. If you're finding that it is cutting down on your enjoyment of the game or if you find that the challenge it presents is too punitive, please do let me know; as I said we are continuing to test and balance it further for the game to be fun while also challenging.

We are working on and will soon be releasing an update with more Senate interactions, followed by updates centered around Rome's wars and expansion and the Roman Client-Patron system. You can read more about these planned updates here: https://steamcommunity.com/app/1063790/discussions/0/2530372519559337823/

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1063790/Citizen_of_Rome__Dynasty_Ascendant/

notes.title: Release, Pricing and Roadmap : Citizen of Rome - Dynasty Ascendant
notes.notes:
[h1]Release[/h1]

We are going to be releasing Citizen of Rome - Dynasty Ascendant on Steam a bit earlier than initially planned, those of you who have already been playing the game either via itch or Google Play have the same latest and most stable version that we will be releasing on Steam.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34903694/7e76b4857b225d8b8a88aa199fbe1d9bdcea3e10.png[/img]

We are going to take it live [u]later today[/u] and the main reasoning behind this earlier release is so that we can also participate in the Steam Summer Sale. We are a small indie team with very limited marketing budget and a limited reach, therefore we need to make use of every opportunity to get the game infront of more people. I am told that participating the Sale will be a great opportunity to do so, and that the originally planned release date would prevent us from participating, due to Steam's 30 day discount cool down.

[h1]Pricing and Discounts[/h1]

We will be releasing it here with a launch discount of 21% and will have the exact same discount in the Summer Sale as well

As a general guideline, we avoid discounts, and in case we do have a sale we will not take the price below this discounted launch price, for the foreseeable future.

We also see the base price going up a few months from now as we add more content and build a further deeper experience in the base game itself

[h1]Roadmap[/h1]

I believe the game in its present state does a decent job of capturing the day to day life, events and social growth in the Roman Republic. We want to make this game the definitive experience of life in Ancient Rome, and will [u]continue to work towards that after today's release, and as long as there is player interest[/u].

The current overarching goal is to allow players to experience the lives, events and deeds of some of Rome's most famous and interesting Citizens, with the likes of the Gracchi Brothers, Caesar, Crassus, Marius, Sulla and more.

To this end, one of the first things we are expanding on is the political and military aspects of the game, in a major update coming a few weeks from now, we will have more Senate interactions, be able to track and contribute to Rome's expansion, events around wars, conscription and its effect on family life, Clients and Patrons, political marriages, and more

I will be detailing these out in multiple Dev Diaries in the coming weeks.

Community feedback and ideas have driving this game from the very beginning and so your voice matters, please do write to us here or on rome@thestartupengine.net with ideas, feedback, criticism, praise or anything else. 

We have prioritized and delivered on various community requests and ideas in the past (including the Dark Mode, Expanding on Ludi, UI, etc), so please do let me know what upcoming feature or aspect of life in Ancient Rome excites you and we could prioritize that next

Thank you for all your support!

http://store.steampowered.com/app/1063790

notes.title: Vinalia Rustica - Event of the day - 14th May 2019
notes.notes:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34903694/14698d096e24cd9ad6da6c93bb2ddd1fa63f4f03.png[/img]

[i]Vinalia Rustica was held on 19th of Sextilis (August). It was originally a rustic Latin harvest festival, celebrating the grape harvest, vegetable growth and fertility. At the Roman Vinalia Rustica, kitchen gardens and market-gardens, and presumably vineyards were dedicated to Venus Obsequens, the oldest known form of Venus. In Roman mythology, it marked the fulfillment of a vow by the ancient Latin allies of Rome's legendary ancestor Aeneas, who promised all wine of the next sacred vintage to Jupiter, in return for victory against the Etruscan tyrant Mezentius.[/i]

[i]Saturnalia is a festival in honour of the god Saturn. This holiday is celebrated with a sacrifice at the Temple of Saturn, in the Forum, and a public banquet, followed by private gift-giving, continual partying, and a carnival atmosphere.

Saturnalia was characterized by role reversals and behavioral license. Slaves are treated to a banquet of the kind usually enjoyed by their masters. Saturnalian license also permitted slaves to disrespect their masters without the threat of a punishment. It was a time for free speech. [i]Lupercalia was a very ancient, possibly pre-Roman pastoral annual festival, observed in the city of Rome on February 15, to avert evil spirits and purify the city, releasing health and fertility. At the Lupercal altar, a male goat (or goats) and a dog (possibly standing in for a wolf) were sacrificed by one or another of the Luperci, under the supervision of the Flamen dialis, Jupiter's chief priest. The sacrificial feast followed, after which the Luperci cut thongs (known as februa) from the flayed skin of the animals, and ran with these, naked or near-naked, along the old Palatine boundary, in an anticlockwise direction around the hill, whipping onlookers. A blessing from these whips was believed to cure childlessness

notes.title: Dev Diary - 1st May 2019 - Citizen of Rome - Dynasty Ascendant
notes.notes:
We are actively working to make Citizen of Rome better, equally in terms of improving existing performance, user interface and in adding new content.

I will be sharing some of the progress we have been making and new key features we have been working on via Dev Diaries such as this one.

Today I want share 3 significant changes:

[h1]1. Performance - Chunked NPC management
[/h1]
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34903694/d36b4b1dd58720a11d7d1a1a321231b9cd64ccef.png[/img]

First, we have upgraded the way the game handles events for non-player-characters - NPCs that are not a part of your household, they still live their lives, have kids, get educated and married on their own, the reason we have this is so that the family of say your character's brother who has a household of their own separately from yours, continues to exist and progress, so that they are available for you to play as in case your character dies heirless. We also use it to generate NPCs for marriage, etc and to marry &/ kill them off later.

The newest update makes it so that these NPCs continue to experience targeted events but changes the way the game handles them, so that only a small set of NPCs are processed every month instead of all of them.

This significantly improves performance, and will be especially noticeable if you are on a low end device or in the late game with a large family and many NPCs around.

[h1]2. Replacing auto-scroll with character notifications
[/h1]
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34903694/479cb2098af5bcbb1f2857cf8e84e6d7de7abc43.png[/img]

Previously the game used to automatically scroll and highlight characters with interesting things happening to them, be it them getting pregnant, being ready for school or winning an election. While this works well for smaller families, it can get irritating when you have a large family with grandchildren and great grandchildren. This also had the effect of slowing the game down with all that scrolling and sometimes even preventing you from doing what you intended to do.

To solve this we have implemented character notifications that show up on the right end of the screen. When hovered upon, they tell you about the update/thing of interest that has happened to a character, and when clicked, they scroll to and highlight the character. These notifications also disappear automatically in a few seconds making interacting with them entirely optional.

[h1]3. Scaling apprenticeship costs based on potential earnings[/h1]
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34903694/9f2c74687691055819e1d0a1790fcd3e9c8cbb6d.png[/img]

Apprentice costs are now scaled based on what you can expect to earn with a given occupation. Previously it was a fixed cost, under the thought process that you were working while apprenticing and thus only paid for tutoring costs, balancing it out with your work. 

But upon looking at it again, I realised having it be a fraction of your future earnings would work better especially in providing a meaningful choice where you only pick the apprenticeship you can actually afford, after weighing your revenues and apprenticeship costs against future earnings.


That's it for now, Citizen of Rome - Dynasty Ascendant is coming soon to Steam with a hefty launch discount, please be sure to wishlist it so that you don't miss out. And feel free to share any thoughts/ideas/suggestions

Long live the Republic!

notes.title: Citizen of Rome - Dynasty Ascendant : Coming Soon to Steam
notes.notes:
Citizen of Rome - Dynasty Ascendant is a sandbox role playing/management offline game where you control a character and their family in the Mid-Republic era of the Roman Republic

Experience life and events in the Roman Republic. Help your family rise to greatness and lead Rome to greater glory. Long live the Republic!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34903694/4898e5507220be47d558060948ad16b980c0d1c6.png[/img]

You get to see how life was in the Ancient Republic, participate in their various customs, festivals and Ludi / sporting competitions, while raising a family and moving up in the social and economic hierarchy in the Republic.

You can educate your children, marry them off, sponsor their elections and much more. You'll usually play as the eldest of your sons once your character dies.

The game is open-ended without a set endgame just like in real life, but a grand goal for any ambitious Roman family was to land a Consulship of the republic. This could be your goal in the game as well, climbing the Cursus Honorum and becoming a "New Man" - "Novus Homo"

Citizen of Rome - Dynasty Ascendant is coming soon to Steam with a hefty launch discount, please be sure to wishlist it so that you don't miss out

Also we are working on adding more historical events and character paths that will let you follow the footsteps of the likes of Caesar, the Gracchi, Cicero, Crassus, Africanus or even Brutus. Follow their footsteps or Forge your own path to greatness!

Long live the Republic!
